newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices fall on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices fall on mild weather.

text.p: Pressured by mild weather throughout many regions of the U.S., spot natural gas prices fell several cents Monday following last week's rally to well above index levels, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas prices slipped more than five cents to the $2.23-2.28 per million British thermal units range, with Transco (Station 65) deals done early in the high-$2.30s.

The continuing heat in the Southwest kept prices from falling significantly in the south Texas markets where traders reported closing deals in the low-$2.20s, down about four cents from Friday's levels.

As temperatures hovered near normal in the Midcontinent, prices eased by about three cents today into the $2.05-2.10 range. Chicago city-gate was quoted in the low-$2.40s, down sharply from Friday's range of $2.55-2.58.

In west Texas, Permian prices were down about four cents into the $2.05-2.07 area as temperatures moderated on the West Coast. Trading at the Waha hub was done in the $2.10-2.13 range, down about five cents.
At the southern California border, prices ranged anywhere from $2.10 to $2.20 in light activity, as compared to the $2.15-2.20 range seen on Friday.
Southern California Edison Co reported earlier Monday that its 1,080 megawatt unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant was back to full power.
Despite the softening of cash prices, temperatures are expected to dip to five to 10 degrees below-normal in the Northeast later this week, boosting incremental demand.
